title: U.S. House · California's 25th District
area: Imperial County and parts of Riverside and San Bernardino counties, including the Coachella Valley (Indio, Coachella, Cathedral City) and Inland Empire and Imperial County cities such as Hemet, San Jacinto, El Centro, Calexico, and Needles. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.
Incumbent Democrat Raul Ruiz advanced from California's June 2, 2026 top-two primary along with Republican Joe Males, a Hemet City Council member.

candidates.name: Raul Ruiz
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, CA-25 (since 2013, representing the 36th District 2013-2023 and the 25th District since 2023)

summary.text: Raul Ruiz is the Democratic incumbent for California's 25th Congressional District. He is an emergency physician who worked in the Coachella Valley and as a senior associate dean at the UC Riverside School of Medicine before winning election to the U.S. House in 2012. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

background.text: Born in Zacatecas, Mexico. According to his official biography, he grew up in Coachella, California, where both of his parents were farmworkers.
Graduated from Coachella Valley High School in 1990 and from UCLA in 1994 (magna cum laude, according to his official biography).

Earned a medical degree and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard University in 2001 and a master's degree in public health from Harvard in 2007. His official biography says he was the first Latino to earn three graduate degrees from Harvard.

Completed a residency in emergency medicine at the University of Pittsburgh and a fellowship in international emergency medicine at Brigham and Women's Hospital; during training he consulted for the health ministries of Serbia and El Salvador.

Returned to the Coachella Valley as an emergency physician at Eisenhower Medical Center, started a pre-medical mentorship program that became part of the UC Riverside School of Medicine, and served there as a senior associate dean. He also helped open a free clinic through Volunteers in Medicine and in 2010 started the Coachella Valley Healthcare Initiative.

In 2010 traveled to Haiti after the earthquake and served as medical director for the J/P Haitian Relief Organization; the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division presented him a Commander's Award for Public Service for that work.
Won election to the U.S. House in 2012 in California's 36th District, defeating Republican Mary Bono Mack, and has been re-elected since; the district number changed to the 25th in 2023.

Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology, Health, and Environment subcommittees in 2025-2026) and previously served on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2021-2022) and the Natural Resources Committee (2013-2016). His official biography says he lives in Indio.

positions.summary: Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and cosponsored the Climate Action Now Act to keep the U.S. on track with Paris Agreement emissions goals.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz also helped bring the Inflation Reduction Act across the finish line, which makes the single largest investment ever in combatting climate change while bringing clean energy manufacturing jobs to local communities.

positions.summary: Authored legislation signed into law to strengthen and expand Medicaid coverage for children and families with mental health needs.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz has also gotten legislation signed into law to strengthen and expand Medicaid.

positions.summary: Supports increased border security funding and technology while also backing a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and farmworkers, opposing their deportation.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz supports securing our borders with smart, modern technology while maintaining professionalism and humanity in our immigration system.

positions.summary: Said families are paying a “tariff tax” at checkout and the pump as a result of the administration's tariffs, marking the one-year anniversary of the April 2025 tariff order.
positions.quote: Families in our valleys are paying the Trump tariff tax every single day, at the checkout line, at the pump, and in small businesses struggling to survive.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology Subcommittee; Health Subcommittee; Environment Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Joe Males

summary.text: Joe Males is the Republican nominee for California's 25th Congressional District. He is a Marine Corps veteran, a computer-networking business owner, and a member of the Hemet City Council, where he is Mayor Pro Tem. His campaign website says he is running to bring leadership and solutions to Washington for the Inland Empire and Imperial County.

background.text: Enlisted in the Marine Corps shortly after turning 18, attended boot camp at Camp Pendleton, and served overseas in the Philippines and Guam before being honorably discharged as a Sergeant.

Worked in computer networking services, starting in an entry-level position and moving through leadership roles; in 1996 he started his own business (JM Consulting, according to the City of Hemet). He and his wife moved to Hemet in 2005.
Volunteered helping seniors with computers and joined the Hemet Elks Lodge 1740 and American Legion Post 53, where the city's biography says he became Post Commander.
According to his campaign website, his entry into politics followed the murder of his son, a Marine, and he ran for Hemet City Council to work on public safety and the rule of law.

Serves on the Hemet City Council representing District 4 and is the city's Mayor Pro Tem. His campaign website says he has led initiatives on infrastructure, business growth, and keeping neighborhoods safe and clean.

priorities.text: Describes his campaign as bringing "Leadership & Commonsense Solutions to Washington for the people of the Inland Empire and Imperial County."
On the Hemet City Council, says he has led initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean.
